title: Enterprise RAG Platform
oneLiner: An on-premises retrieval-augmented generation system for secure enterprise knowledge access, with zero external data exposure.
problem: Enterprise teams needed conversational access to internal documentation, but sending proprietary data to third-party LLM APIs was a non-starter for security and compliance.
background: Built during an AI internship at KONE's Enterprise Innovation Team, where the baseline was a keyword-search system across a large internal document set.
architecture: Documents are parsed and chunked, embedded, and indexed in a FAISS vector store. A LangChain-orchestrated retrieval layer serves relevant chunks to an on-prem LLM for conversational answers — the entire pipeline runs inside the enterprise network with no data leaving the perimeter.
challenges: Keeping the entire retrieval and inference pipeline on-premises while maintaining response quality comparable to hosted LLM APIs.
Tuning chunking and retrieval parameters so relevance improved measurably over the existing keyword-search baseline.
lessons: Retrieval quality is often the real bottleneck in RAG systems, not the generation model — most of the latency and relevance gains came from getting chunking, indexing, and retrieval right before touching the LLM layer.
futureWork: Extending ingestion to more document types and adding structured evaluation for retrieval quality over time.

title: Offline Mapping & Navigation System
oneLiner: An offline geospatial navigation pipeline that distinguishes highway vs. service-road movement without any live connectivity.
problem: Reliable navigation in low-connectivity regions requires movement classification that doesn't depend on live map or GPS-quality data.
background: Built for Smart India Hackathon 2024, where the team reached the national final.
architecture: Uses tile maps, heading vectors, and coordinate clustering algorithms to detect whether a device is moving along a highway or a parallel service road, entirely offline.
challenges: Distinguishing highway vs. service-road movement using only coordinate and heading data, without live map matching.
lessons: Classical geospatial clustering techniques can substitute effectively for connectivity-dependent map matching when engineered carefully.
futureWork: Expanding the classifier to more road topologies and integrating it into a full offline navigation app.

title: Climate Detection Using AI
oneLiner: A CNN-based climate classification model with a custom preprocessing and evaluation pipeline, published as research.
problem: Automating climate/weather-pattern classification from image data for downstream research use.
background: Co-authored as one of two academic research papers published at IJITRA during the CSE (AI & ML) program.
architecture: A convolutional neural network trained on a custom preprocessing pipeline, with a dedicated evaluation harness for measuring classification performance.
challenges: Building a clean preprocessing pipeline for noisy, varied climate imagery.
lessons: Investing time in preprocessing and evaluation infrastructure paid off more than iterating on model architecture alone.
futureWork: Extending the dataset and benchmarking against additional model architectures.
